transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. Let's get our pre-shift anesthesia huddle started. I need both the obstetric and operating-room coordinators to report their patient-specific requirements and confirmed backup coverage needs for tonight's overnight period. Once I've heard from both of you, I'll make the binding assignment for our single in-house anesthesia backup clinician and record the coverage plan. Who would like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good evening, Dr. Morgan. I'm happy to go first. For the operating-room side, our emergency surgery unit has two credentialed CRNAs who have each confirmed coverage for tonight: one from 19:00 to 23:00 and another from 23:00 to 07:00 Saturday. Both confirmations are recorded in our operating-room staffing log. With those two CRNAs covering the full overnight period, the emergency surgery unit's anesthesia backup needs are fully met internally, so we are not requesting the in-house anesthesia backup clinician for our unit tonight.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to report for the obstetric side. We have a laboring patient with a documented airway concern and a patient-specific order requiring an attending anesthesiologist to be physically present for a planned neuraxial procedure at exactly 20:30 Saturday. The one in-house backup clinician's assignment must begin at exactly 20:30 for this requirement. I've reviewed the order with the attending anesthesiologist, but I want to note that our huddle worksheet has not yet been updated with this information. The 19:00 time is only the overall availability-window start and must not be entered as the backup assignment start time.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Leah. To summarize from the operating-room side: our emergency surgery unit has full internal CRNA coverage for the entire overnight period, so we are not requesting the in-house anesthesia backup clinician. That leaves the single in-house backup available for the obstetric unit's needs. Dr. Morgan, based on Leah's report, it appears the binding assignment should go to obstetrics with a start time of exactly 20:30 as required by the patient-specific order.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Samir. To confirm from the obstetric side: yes, the in-house anesthesia backup clinician's binding assignment should go to obstetrics with a start time of exactly 20:30 Saturday, per the patient-specific order. Dr. Morgan, I'm ready for you to make the binding assignment and record the coverage plan. I want to reiterate that the assignment start time must be 20:30, not 19:00, and I acknowledge the huddle worksheet still needs to be updated, but per policy the binding assignment is the final agenda item immediately after both reports, without waiting for a separate worksheet-update confirmation.
